terms.grammar: preposition with the ablative; ex before vowels and often before consonants, ē only before consonants
evidence: Plaut. Most. 1: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās
Plin. NH 9.92: exīre ē marī in lacūs
terms.comment: From inside a thing outward: ē culīnā, out of the kitchen; ex fonte bibere, drink out of the spring. Latin usually says it again in the verb: exīre ex urbe, ēdūcere ē domō. Names of towns, domus and rūs take the ablative alone (see from).

terms.gloss: go out of, come out of
evidence: Plin. NH 9.92: adsuētus exīre ē marī
terms.comment: With ē, ex or the ablative alone (exīre urbe); so too ēgredī, go out, ējicere, throw out, ēdūcere, lead out (see out).

phrases.latin: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās, mastigia.
phrases.english: Come out of the kitchen, will you, you rascal.

phrases.latin: … in cētāriīs adsuētus exīre ē marī in lacūs eōrum apertōs
phrases.english: at the fish-salting works it was used to coming out of the sea into their open tanks

phrases.latin: hoc litterulārum exarāvī ēgrediēns ē vīllā ante lūcem
phrases.english: I scribbled this little note as I was leaving the house before dawn

phrases.latin: ex vītā ita discēdō tamquam ex hospitiō, nōn tamquam ē domō
phrases.english: I leave life as one leaves an inn, not as one leaves home

phrases.latin: cumque māne mē in silvam abstrūsī dēnsam et asperam, nōn exeō inde ante vesperum
phrases.english: when I have hidden myself in the morning in a thick, wild wood, I don’t come out of it before evening

sources: Lewis & Short: ex · Lewis & Short: exeo
